title: Pin Classes I: Growth Rates: the growth rate of the box-plus class as a limit over tails
author: Ben Jarvis
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Proposition (source0.tex lines 4069--4074, source label limprop): for a pin class generated by an infinite pin word and the corresponding box-plus class, the limit as n tends to infinity of the growth rate of the box-plus of the n-th tail of the word equals the growth rate of the box-plus class of the word; the article presents this as the remarkable statement that two of its earlier inequalities are in fact equalities, and it is the step that pins down the growth rate of the box-plus class. It is delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 4076--4136 (one adjacent proof environment of 61 lines that opens and closes inside the retained span). The proof is complete and closed inside the retained span together with its retained context: it compares the two growth rates through the retained description of the box-plus class, uses the retained identification of the growth rate of the class with a supremum of convergence radii of generating functions, and applies the retained Finite Prefix Lemma to transfer the finite-prefix information along the tails, obtaining both inequalities and hence the equality of the limit with the growth rate. H2: a research-level enumerative-combinatorics proposition about pin classes, box-plus operations and exponential growth rates, whose proof combines the finite-prefix structure of pin words, the algebra of the box-plus operation on classes and an analytic comparison of growth rates through generating functions; it is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises.
